verdict.reasoning: Patient says: 'my chest has been feeling really tight' and later clarifies duration: 'for about... three hours now.'

Mild SOB: 'Yeah, like a little bit... a little bit short of breath, not too bad.' Wheeze: 'I'm feeling a bit wheezy.' Dry (non-productive) cough and slightly worse at night: 'Are you coughing up anything?' 'Uh, no.' and 'Is the cough worse at night-time?' 'it gets a little bit worse at night but... pretty consistent.' Unable to take full breath: 'It just feels like sometimes, I can't get a full breath in.'
Doctor: 'you wouldn't say you've got chest pains? It's more of a tight chest, is it?' Patient: 'No, not really pain, it's more like, tight.'

Patient: 'You know I had a cold last week... I had a sore throat, I had a runny nose... Are you feeling better now, other than the tight chest?' Patient: 'the runny nose isn't as bad any more.' This is consistent with a recent viral URTI now improving.

Asthma: 'Yeah, yeah, I have asthma, I've had it for a while now.' Hay fever and dust allergy: 'then I have like, a hayfever, you know, and some allergies just to dust.' Childhood eczema and milk-protein allergy: 'my mum has eczema, and my dad has asthma... when I was young, I also had eczema. And I had a milk protein allergy, when I was young too.'
Severe exacerbation with intubation: 'when I was in high school, I had to have a tube put down my throat.' Age 16–17: 'I think I was like seventeen. Sixteen maybe.'

Medications: 'the um, uh, Ventolin. It's called uh, Salbutamol... and then I have a steroid, a Clenil, Clenil inhaler.' Supply lapse 1 week: 'I forgot to bring it with me, so I haven't really in the past week... they ran out and I, I forgot to, go and grab the next one... About a week ago.' Doctor confirms: 'you haven't got any Clenil, or any Ventolin at the moment?' Patient: 'Not with me right now, no, I ran out.'

Dust allergy and no drug allergy: 'I have like, a hayfever, you know, and some allergies just to dust' and later: 'any drug allergies, that you know of?' Patient: 'No, no, not allergic to anything. Just like, just the, dust and stuff, but nothing, no drugs.'
Patient: 'my mum has eczema, and my dad has asthma.'
Patient: 'I was away at uni last week.' This supports that he is a university student.

Acute asthma exacerbation: Doctor repeatedly refers to 'this asthma attack' and gives steroids/inhalers. Precipitant viral URTI: recent cold last week with sore throat/runny nose and ongoing cough/wheeze. Missed preventer: 'I forgot to bring it with me, so I haven't really in the past week... they ran out and I forgot to go and grab the next one.' This is a standard clinical inference.
Medication supply lapse and non-adherence: 'they ran out and I, I forgot to, go and grab the next one... About a week ago' and 'I forgot to bring it with me, so I haven't really in the past week.'

Doctor: 'give you a, dose of steroids. So this is, these are tablets which, you can take for five days. Uh, two tablets in the morning.' While the name Prednisolone is not said, oral steroid tablets for 5 days, 2 each morning, matches the content.

Prescription and PRN advice: 'give you a prescription for, uh, some more of the inhalers.' and 'you can... use the Clenil Modulite in the morning, with Ventolin as a PRN... a Ventolin when you need to.' Usage threshold: 'If you should start to use the Ventolin more than, uh, every three hours... it's a good idea to seek medical attention.'

Doctor: 'send you these, the, some prescriptions for your, uh, inhalers, ongoing... once you get better from this asthma attack, you can, you can, use the Clenil Modulite in the morning, with Ventolin as a PRN.' This resumes maintenance Clenil.

Spacer and technique: 'the other thing I'd like to send you is a spacer... I'll send you another one, and it has some instructions about how to use it, but essentially, uh, couple of puffs to prime it, inside, breathing in and out, um, uh, for five or ten breaths.'

Rest and sick leave: 'I might give you some time off work as well. You can self-certify first seven days, but uh, I think I would advise you just to, rest a little bit until you're feeling a bit better.'

Safety-net: 'Any deterioration in your symptoms, like worsening shortness of breath. Um, or just generally concerning symptoms, uh, pain in your chest tightness, uh, feeling light-headed. Uh, then, seek further medical attention anytime please.' This covers increased SOB, chest pain/tightness, dizziness, and need for urgent care.
The transcript does not mention arranging any specific follow-up appointment or review after the steroid course; only general advice to seek medical attention if symptoms worsen.
